title: Classifying multipartite continuous-variable entanglement structures through data-augmented neural networks - Nature Machine Intelligence
gist: A Peking University-led team shows that a convolutional neural network fed only with binned homodyne-detection correlation patterns can classify multipartite continuous-variable entanglement structures, and that physics-derived quantum data augmentation (mode permutation plus convex combination of separable states) lifts accuracy from 0.961 to 0.986 for tripartite states and 0.796 to 0.928 for quadripartite states. The method substitutes cheap synthetic-data tricks for prohibitively expensive quantum state tomography, but the authors concede that scaling beyond five modes runs into a hard compute budget.
